*Describe merging `incoming` into the current branch, without changing
anything.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'a.txt': 'a\n'}))
sh(r.root, 'branch', 'other')
commit(r.root, 'ours', a__txt='ours\n')
r.checkout('other')
commit(r.root, 'theirs', b__txt='b\n')
head = r._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD')

prev = r.merge_preview('main')
test_eq((prev['conflicts'], prev['conflict_likely']), ([], False))
test_eq(r._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD'), head)              # rehearsing moved nothing
test_eq(r.rebase_preview('main')['conflicts'], [])
test_eq(r.rebase_preview('main')['already_based'], False)
cmp = r.compare('main', 'other')                        # whole trees, not the merge base
test_eq(cmp['changed_files'], 2)
test_eq((cmp['left_only'], cmp['right_only']), (1, 1))
assert 'b.txt' in cmp['patch'] and 'a.txt' in cmp['patch']

c = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'shared.txt': 'base\n'}))
sh(c.root, 'branch', 'other')
commit(c.root, 'ours', shared__txt='ours\n')
c.checkout('other')
commit(c.root, 'theirs', shared__txt='theirs\n')
test_eq(c.merge_preview('main')['conflicts'], ['shared.txt'])
test_eq(c.merge_preview('main')['conflict_likely'], True)
test_eq(c._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD'), c._ask('rev-parse', 'other'))
```

## Resolving one conflict

`conflict_versions` returns the versions of a conflicted file: `base`,
the common ancestor; `ours` and `theirs`, the two sides; and `worktree`,
the file on disk with its conflict markers. `conflict_versions` raises
[`GitError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#giterror)
when the file is not conflicted.
`resolve_conflict(path, choice, content=None)` settles the file and then
stages it. `choice` is `'ours'`, `'theirs'`, `'worktree'` (keep the
working-tree file as it is) or `'resolved'`, which writes `content` to
the file first. `resolve_conflict` raises
[`GitError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#giterror)
for any other choice and for `'resolved'` without `content`. The result
lists the files still conflicted in `conflicted`, and has a one-sentence
`summary`.

During a merge, `ours` is the branch you have checked out and `theirs`
is the branch coming in.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1391"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.resolve_conflict

``` python
def resolve_conflict(
    path, choice, content:NoneType=None
):
```

*Settle one conflicted file and stage it as resolved.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1380"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.conflict_versions

``` python
def conflict_versions(
    path
):
```

*The base, ours, theirs and working-tree versions of the conflicted file
`path`.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'shared.txt': 'base\n'}))
sh(r.root, 'branch', 'other')
commit(r.root, 'ours', shared__txt='ours\n')
r.checkout('other')
commit(r.root, 'theirs', shared__txt='theirs\n')
r.merge('main')

v = r.conflict_versions('shared.txt')
test_eq((v['ours'], v['theirs'], v['base']), ('theirs\n', 'ours\n', 'base\n'))

out = r.resolve_conflict('shared.txt', 'ours')
test_eq((r.root/'shared.txt').read_text(), 'theirs\n')
test_eq(out['conflicted'], [])
test_eq(out['operation']['active'], 'merge')            # resolved, but not yet committed
assert 'every conflict is resolved' in out['summary']
r.operation_action('abort')

r.merge('main')
r.resolve_conflict('shared.txt', 'theirs')
test_eq((r.root/'shared.txt').read_text(), 'ours\n')
r.operation_action('abort')

r.merge('main')
r.resolve_conflict('shared.txt', 'resolved', 'decided by hand\n')
test_eq((r.root/'shared.txt').read_text(), 'decided by hand\n')
r.operation_action('abort')

r.merge('main')
test_fail(lambda: r.resolve_conflict('shared.txt', 'nonsense'), contains='conflict choice must be')
test_fail(lambda: r.resolve_conflict('shared.txt', 'resolved'), contains='resolved contents')
test_fail(lambda: r.conflict_versions('readme.md'), contains='is not conflicted')
r.operation_action('abort')
```

## Planning conflict resolution

A conflict block whose two sides are identical needs no decision.
`resolve_safe_conflicts(paths=())` removes the markers around such
blocks, keeping the shared text, for the files in `paths` or for every
conflicted file when `paths` is empty. It stages a file once none of its
blocks remain. Blocks whose sides differ are left for a person. It
returns the files it changed in `resolved` and a fresh `plan`.
`conflict_plan` lists the conflicted files with how many blocks each
has, how many of those are `safe` (identical sides) and how many need a
person (`manual`). A file whose working-tree text contains a NUL
character counts as binary. It has `kind` `binary` and needs one whole
side chosen.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1431"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.resolve_safe_conflicts

``` python
def resolve_safe_conflicts(
    paths:tuple=()
):
```

*Remove only conflict markers whose ours and theirs text is identical,
then stage.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1410"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.conflict_plan

``` python
def conflict_plan():
```

*Unresolved files with deterministic marker-level resolution
suggestions.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'shared.txt': 'base\n'}))
sh(r.root, 'branch', 'other')
commit(r.root, 'ours', shared__txt='ours\n')
r.checkout('other')
commit(r.root, 'theirs', shared__txt='theirs\n')
r.merge('main')

plan = r.conflict_plan()
test_eq([f['path'] for f in plan['files']], ['shared.txt'])
test_eq(plan['operation']['active'], 'merge')
test_eq(plan['files'][0]['kind'], 'text')
test_eq((plan['files'][0]['blocks'], plan['files'][0]['safe']), (1, 0))
test_eq(plan['summary'], {'files': 1, 'blocks': 1, 'safe': 0, 'manual': 1})

# Two sides that genuinely differ are nobody's to resolve automatically, so nothing is taken.
test_eq(r.resolve_safe_conflicts()['resolved'], [])
test_eq([f['path'] for f in r.resolve_safe_conflicts()['plan']['files']], ['shared.txt'])

# A block whose two sides say the same thing is safe, and taking it stages the file.
s = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'both.txt': 'a\nb\nc\n'}))
sh(s.root, 'branch', 'other')
commit(s.root, 'ours', both__txt='a\nb\nOURS\n')
s.checkout('other')
commit(s.root, 'theirs', both__txt='a\nb\nTHEIRS\n')
s.merge('main')
marked = s._version('both.txt', 'worktree')
block, = _conflict_blocks(marked)
s.write_worktree('both.txt', marked[:block['start']] + '<<<<<<< HEAD\nsame\n=======\nsame\n'
                 '>>>>>>> main\n' + marked[block['end']:])
done = s.resolve_safe_conflicts()
test_eq([x['path'] for x in done['resolved']], ['both.txt'])
test_eq((done['resolved'][0]['safe'], done['resolved'][0]['remaining']), (1, 0))
test_eq(done['plan']['files'], [])
test_eq((s.root/'both.txt').read_text(), 'a\nb\nsame\n')

r.operation_action('abort')
test_eq(r.conflict_plan()['files'], [])                 # nothing in progress, nothing to decide
```

## Blame

`blame` says which commit last changed each line of a file, with its
author, time and summary line. `blame(path, start=1, end=0)` returns one
row per line with the keys `oid`, `line`, `original_line`, `author`,
`timestamp`, `summary` and `text`. `start` and `end` limit it to a range
of lines. The default `end=0` means the whole file, and `start` has no
effect then.

``` python
rows = r.blame('a.txt')
test_eq(len(rows), 2)
test_eq(rows[0]['author'], 'Repo tests')
test_eq(rows[0]['line'], 1)
test_eq(rows[0]['summary'], 'initial')
test_eq(r.blame('a.txt', 2, 2)[0]['line'], 2)
test_eq(len(r.blame('a.txt', 1, 1)), 1)

commit(r.root, 'change the second line', a__txt='one\nTWO\n')
test_eq([x['summary'] for x in r.blame('a.txt')], ['initial', 'change the second line'])
```

## Worktrees and submodules

A worktree is an extra checkout of the same repository in another
folder, usually with a different branch checked out. A submodule is
another repository embedded in this one at a fixed commit. `worktrees`
lists the checkouts, one row each with `path`, `head`, `branch` and the
flags `bare`, `detached` and `locked`.
`add_worktree(path, branch='', create=False)` creates one, and with
`create=True` it creates `branch` too.
`remove_worktree(path, force=False)` deletes one, and `force=True`
deletes it even with uncommitted changes. `submodules` lists the
submodules, one row each with `path`, `oid` (the commit it is at),
`state` (the one-character prefix of `git submodule status`) and
`description`. It returns an empty list when the repository has no
submodules.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1510"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

## The diff itself

`diff` returns `git diff` output for the unstaged changes, for the
staged ones with `staged=True`, or between refs. With both `left` and
`right` it compares the merge base of the two with `right`, as
`git diff left...right` does. With `left` alone it compares `left` with
the working tree or, with `staged=True`, with the index. `path` limits
it to one file, and `context` sets how many unchanged lines appear
around each change, from 0 to 20.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1525"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.diff

``` python
def diff(
    path:str='', staged:bool=False, left:str='', right:str='', context:int=3
):
```

*The `git diff` text for unstaged changes, staged ones, or between refs,
for one `path` when given.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'a.txt': 'one\n'}))
write(r.root, 'a.txt', 'two\n')
assert '+two' in r.diff('a.txt')
test_eq(r.diff('a.txt', staged=True), '')
r.stage(['a.txt'])
assert '+two' in r.diff('a.txt', staged=True)
test_eq(r.diff('a.txt'), '')                            # staged, so nothing left unstaged
test_eq(r._version('a.txt', 'index'), 'two\n')          # ...which is where the index now is
test_eq(r._version('a.txt', 'head'), 'one\n')

base = r._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD')
commit(r.root, 'second', a__txt='three\n')
assert '+three' in r.diff('a.txt', left=base, right='HEAD')
```

## Rendering notebooks and LFS pointers

`diff_view(path, staged=False)` prepares one file’s uncommitted changes
for a side-by-side view. It returns a dictionary with the keys `text`
(the raw diff), `content` (the diff to display), `left` and `right` (the
two versions), the flags `notebook` and `binary`, and `lfs` (the pointer
details, or `None`). A notebook is a JSON file, and a diff of its raw
text is hard to read. For a notebook, `left` and `right` are the cell
sources one after another, each cell under a `# %% kind · cell n` line,
and `content` is the diff between those. A file stored in Git LFS
appears to Git as a short pointer file. `diff_view` marks it `binary`
and returns the pointer’s object id and size in `lfs`. It does not
compare two pointers. A binary file has empty `left`, `right` and
`content`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1556"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.diff_view

``` python
def diff_view(
    path, staged:bool=False
):
```

*One file’s unstaged changes, or staged ones with `staged=True`, as a
diff and two versions to show side by side.*

``` python
nb = json.dumps({'cells': [{'cell_type': 'code', 'source': ['x = 1\n']},
                           {'cell_type': 'markdown', 'source': '# heading'}]})
flat = _notebook_content(nb)
assert 'x = 1' in flat and '# heading' in flat and '# %% code' in flat
test_eq(_notebook_content(''), '')
test_eq(_notebook_content('not json'), 'not json')      # not a notebook, so left alone

test_eq(_lfs_pointer(LFS_MAGIC + '\noid sha256:abc\nsize 12\n'), {'oid': 'sha256:abc', 'size': '12'})
test_eq(_lfs_pointer('ordinary text'), None)
test_eq(_lfs_pointer(''), None)

r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'a.txt': 'one\n'}))
write(r.root, 'a.txt', 'two\n')
view = r.diff_view('a.txt')
test_eq((view['left'], view['right']), ('one\n', 'two\n'))
test_eq((view['binary'], view['lfs'], view['notebook']), (False, None, False))

write(r.root, 'new.txt', 'fresh\n')
fresh = r.diff_view('new.txt')
test_eq((fresh['left'], fresh['right']), ('', 'fresh\n'))   # untracked: nothing on the left
assert '+fresh' in fresh['text']

nb = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'n.ipynb': json.dumps({'cells': [{'id': 'a', 'cell_type': 'code',
                                                          'source': 'x = 1\n'}]}, indent=1)}))
write(nb.root, 'n.ipynb', json.dumps({'cells': [{'id': 'a', 'cell_type': 'code',
                                                 'source': 'x = 2\n'}]}, indent=1))
view = nb.diff_view('n.ipynb')
test_eq(view['notebook'], True)
test_eq((view['left'], view['right']), ('# %% code \u00b7 cell 1\nx = 1\n', '# %% code \u00b7 cell 1\nx = 2\n'))
```

## Notebooks

`notebook_changes` says which cells of a notebook differ from `HEAD`,
and which lines inside each, so an editor can mark the changed cells. It
returns a dictionary with `path`, `changed`, `cells` (each changed cell
id mapped to `added` or `modified`) and `lines` (each changed cell id
mapped to its changed line ranges). A deleted cell is not reported. A
path that is not a `.ipynb` file, or has no changes, gives `changed`
false. Cells are matched by their id. Editing one cell therefore does
not make every cell after it look changed.
[`_cells`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#_cells) reads
a notebook’s sources keyed by cell id, or by position for a cell with no
id.
[`_line_ranges`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#_line_ranges)
finds the changed lines inside one cell, as 1-based ranges of kind
`added`, `modified` or `deleted`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1603"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.notebook_changes

``` python
def notebook_changes(
    path
):
```

*Which cells of a notebook differ from HEAD, and which lines within
them.*

``` python
nb = json.dumps({'cells': [{'id': 'a', 'cell_type': 'code', 'source': 'x = 1\n'},
                           {'cell_type': 'code', 'source': ['y', ' = 2\n']}]})
test_eq(_cells(nb), {'a': 'x = 1\n', '#1': 'y = 2\n'})   # a cell with no id is keyed by position
test_eq(_cells('not json'), {})

test_eq(_line_ranges('a\n', 'a\n'), [])
test_eq(_line_ranges('a\n', 'a\nb\n'), [{'from': 2, 'to': 2, 'kind': 'added'}])
test_eq(_line_ranges('a\nb\n', 'a\nB\n'), [{'from': 2, 'to': 2, 'kind': 'modified'}])
# a deletion has no line of its own in `after`, so it is marked at the line that took its place
test_eq(_line_ranges('a\nb\n', 'a\n'), [{'from': 1, 'to': 1, 'kind': 'deleted'}])
test_eq(_line_ranges('a\n', ''), [{'from': 1, 'to': 1, 'kind': 'deleted'}])
test_eq(_line_ranges('a\nb\nc\n', 'a\nb\nc\nd\ne\n'), [{'from': 4, 'to': 5, 'kind': 'added'}])

before = json.dumps({'cells': [{'id': 'a', 'cell_type': 'code', 'source': 'x = 1\n'},
                               {'id': 'b', 'cell_type': 'code', 'source': 'y = 2\n'}]}, indent=1)
after = json.dumps({'cells': [{'id': 'a', 'cell_type': 'code', 'source': 'x = 99\n'},
                              {'id': 'b', 'cell_type': 'code', 'source': 'y = 2\n'}]}, indent=1)
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'n.ipynb': before}))
test_eq(r.notebook_changes('n.ipynb')['changed'], False)
write(r.root, 'n.ipynb', after)
out = r.notebook_changes('n.ipynb')
test_eq(out['changed'], True)
test_eq(sorted(out['cells']), ['a'])                    # only the cell that moved
test_eq(out['lines']['a'], [{'from': 1, 'to': 1, 'kind': 'modified'}])
test_eq(r.notebook_changes('a.txt')['changed'], False)   # not a notebook, so nothing to say
```

## Reading a patch

A unified diff is made of hunks, separate blocks that each start with an
`@@` line.
[`_patch_hunks`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#_patch_hunks)
splits one file’s diff into its hunks and returns one record for each
hunk. The keys are `index`, `from` and `to` (the lines the hunk covers
in the new file), `kind` (`added`, `deleted` or `modified`), `old` and
`new` (the removed and added text) and `patch`, a patch that applies on
its own. Staging or discarding a single hunk uses that patch.

``` python
diff = ('diff --git a/a.txt b/a.txt\n--- a/a.txt\n+++ b/a.txt\n'
        '@@ -1,2 +1,3 @@\n a\n-b\n+B\n+c\n')
hunks = _patch_hunks(diff)
test_eq(len(hunks), 1)
test_eq((hunks[0]['from'], hunks[0]['to']), (2, 3))
test_eq(_patch_hunks(''), [])
test_eq(_patch_hunks('not a diff\n'), [])

two = _patch_hunks('@@ -1 +1 @@\n-a\n+A\n@@ -10,2 +10,2 @@\n-b\n+B\n')
test_eq([(h['from'], h['to'], h['kind']) for h in two], [(1, 1, 'modified'), (10, 10, 'modified')])
test_eq(two[0]['old'], 'a\n')
test_eq(two[0]['new'], 'A\n')
# A hunk that only deletes has no added line to sit on, so it anchors above the deletion.
test_eq([(h['from'], h['to'], h['kind']) for h in _patch_hunks('@@ -5,2 +4,1 @@\n a\n-b\n')],
        [(4, 4, 'deleted')])
```

## Changed lines in one file

`file_changes` gives an editor what it needs to mark changed lines in
the margin of an open file: the line ranges added, modified or deleted
since `HEAD` (`ranges`), the hunks, the full diff, and the file’s status
row (`status`). An untracked file has one `added` range from the first
line to the last, and empty `hunks` and `diff`. A file with no changes
gives `changed` false and no `status`. In a repository with no commits,
`file_changes` compares with the index.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1656"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.file_changes

``` python
def file_changes(
    path
):
```

*The changed line ranges, hunks and diff of `path` compared with
`HEAD`.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'a.txt': 'a\nb\n'}))
test_eq(r.file_changes('a.txt')['changed'], False)
test_eq(r.file_changes('missing.txt'), {'path': 'missing.txt', 'changed': False,
                                        'ranges': [], 'hunks': [], 'diff': ''})

write(r.root, 'a.txt', 'a\nB\nc\n')
out = r.file_changes('a.txt')
test_eq(len(out['hunks']), 1)
test_eq(out['ranges'], [{'from': 2, 'to': 3, 'kind': 'modified'}])
assert out['diff'] and out['status']

write(r.root, 'new.txt', 'fresh\n')
untracked = r.file_changes('new.txt')
test_eq(untracked['hunks'], [])                         # nothing to diff against
test_eq(untracked['ranges'], [{'from': 1, 'to': 1, 'kind': 'added'}])
```

## Replaying a branch in memory

A rebase rewrites history. `_replay` shows what a rebase would do
without rewriting anything. It merges each of your commits onto the
previous result with `git merge-tree` and wraps the result in a new
commit with `git commit-tree`. Both commands only add objects to Git’s
object store. They touch no branch, index or working tree. `_replay`
stops at the first commit that would conflict, which is where a real
rebase would stop. It returns three values: the commit it stopped at
(`oid` and `subject`, or `None`), the number of commits replayed, and
the conflicted files.

`SYNC_OPS` names the four ways `sync` can bring a branch level with its
upstream. `REMOTE_OPS` names the three commands that talk to a remote.
`STATE_KEYS` lists eight keys of the `info` dictionary: `root`,
`branch`, `upstream`, `ahead`, `behind`, `clean`, `branches` and
`changes`.
[`_short_commits`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#_short_commits)
formats up to 20 commits as `short subject` lines.
[`_said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#_said) returns
the `summary` or `message` of a result dictionary, or the stripped text
of any other value. `_upstream` returns the upstream you name, or the
one the branch tracks, and raises
[`GitError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#giterror)
when there is neither.

``` python
test_eq(_short_commits([{'short': 'abc1234', 'subject': 'a subject'}]), ['abc1234 a subject'])
test_eq(_short_commits([{'short': 'a', 'subject': 'x'}] * 30), ['a x'] * 20)   # capped for a summary
test_eq(_said({'summary': 's'}), 's')
test_eq(_said({'message': 'm'}), 'm')
test_eq(_said(' text '), 'text')
test_eq(_said(None), '')
test_eq(sorted(SYNC_OPS), ['fast-forward', 'merge', 'rebase', 'reset'])
test_eq(REMOTE_OPS, ('fetch', 'pull', 'push'))

r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'a.txt': 'base\n'}))
test_fail(lambda: r._upstream(), contains='tracks nothing')
sh(r.root, 'branch', 'other')
commit(r.root, 'ours', b__txt='b\n')
onto = r._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD')
r.checkout('other')
commit(r.root, 'theirs', c__txt='c\n')
head = r._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD')

stops, replayed, files = r._replay(onto, list(reversed(r.history(ref=f'{onto}..HEAD'))))
test_eq((stops, replayed, files), (None, 1, []))        # replays cleanly
test_eq(r._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD'), head)              # ...and moved nothing

c = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'shared.txt': 'base\n'}))
sh(c.root, 'branch', 'other')
commit(c.root, 'ours', shared__txt='ours\n')
onto = c._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD')
c.checkout('other')
commit(c.root, 'theirs', shared__txt='theirs\n')
stops, replayed, files = c._replay(onto, list(reversed(c.history(ref=f'{onto}..HEAD'))))
test_eq(stops['subject'], 'theirs')                     # the commit a rebase would stop at
test_eq((replayed, files), (0, ['shared.txt']))
```

## Choosing a synchronization strategy

`divergence(upstream='', fetch=False)` compares the current branch with
its upstream, or with a branch you name, and `relation` says how they
stand: `identical`, `ahead`, `behind` or `diverged`. With `fetch=True`
it fetches first. It raises
[`GitError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#giterror)
when the branch tracks nothing and you name no upstream, and when the
two share no merge base. The counts `ahead` and `behind` are exact
however many commits there are, while `ours` and `theirs` list at most
20 commits each.

`divergence` then rehearses each way of bringing the branch level. A
fast-forward is possible when you have no commits of your own. A merge
or a reset is possible whenever the upstream has commits you lack. A
rebase is possible when both sides have commits. The merge is rehearsed
with `merge-tree` and the rebase with `_replay`. The `merge` and
`rebase` options list the files they would conflict on. The options that
rewrite history, `rebase` and `reset`, are marked `destructive`.

`recommended` is a fast-forward when you have no commits of your own.
When both sides have commits, it is a rebase if your commits replay
without conflict and no tracked file has uncommitted changes. Otherwise
it is a merge. It is empty when the upstream has nothing you lack.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1723"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.divergence

``` python
def divergence(
    upstream:str='', fetch:bool=False
):
```

*You against your upstream, every way back rehearsed before any of them
runs.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'a.txt': 'base\n'}))
bare = mkbare()
sh(r.root, 'remote', 'add', 'origin', str(bare))
sh(r.root, 'push', '-u', 'origin', 'main')
test_eq(r._upstream(), 'origin/main')

d = r.divergence()
test_eq(d['relation'], 'identical')
test_eq((d['ahead'], d['behind'], d['recommended']), (0, 0, ''))
test_eq(sorted(o['op'] for o in d['options']), sorted(SYNC_OPS))

other = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); _tmp.append(str(other))
o = GitRepo.at(clone(str(bare), other, 'other'))
sh(o.root, 'config', 'user.email', 'tests@example.com')
sh(o.root, 'config', 'user.name', 'Repo tests')
commit(o.root, 'upstream moved', b__txt='b\n')
o.push()

r.fetch()
test_eq(r.divergence()['relation'], 'behind')
test_eq(r.divergence()['recommended'], 'fast-forward')

commit(r.root, 'we moved', c__txt='c\n')
d = r.divergence()
test_eq((d['relation'], d['ahead'], d['behind']), ('diverged', 1, 1))
test_eq(d['recommended'], 'rebase')                     # nothing rehearsed a conflict
test_eq({x['op']: x['available'] for x in d['options']}['fast-forward'], False)
test_eq({x['op']: x for x in d['options']}['rebase']['stops_at'], None)
test_eq(d['ours'], ['%s we moved' % r._ask('rev-parse', '--short', 'HEAD')])
```

## Doing it

`sync(how='rebase', upstream='')` carries out one of the four options in
`SYNC_OPS` as a guarded change. It raises
[`GitError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#giterror)
for any other `how`. For a rebase or a reset it sets uncommitted work
aside first and brings it back afterwards. A fast-forward and a merge do
not set work aside. A reset runs `git reset --hard`. It discards your
own commits, and `undo` can bring them back.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1758"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.sync

``` python
def sync(
    how:str='rebase', upstream:str=''
):
```

*Reconcile with the upstream the way `divergence` rehearsed.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'a.txt': 'base\n'}))
bare = mkbare()
sh(r.root, 'remote', 'add', 'origin', str(bare))
sh(r.root, 'push', '-u', 'origin', 'main')
other = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); _tmp.append(str(other))
o = GitRepo.at(clone(str(bare), other, 'other'))
sh(o.root, 'config', 'user.email', 'tests@example.com')
sh(o.root, 'config', 'user.name', 'Repo tests')
commit(o.root, 'upstream moved', b__txt='b\n')
o.push()
commit(r.root, 'we moved', c__txt='c\n')
r.fetch()

test_fail(lambda: r.sync('sideways'), contains='sync must be one of')
test_eq(r.sync('rebase')['op'], 'rebase')
test_eq(r.divergence()['relation'], 'ahead')
r.push()
test_eq(r.divergence(fetch=True)['relation'], 'identical')

# ...and a divergence that would conflict recommends the merge instead.
o.pull()
commit(o.root, 'theirs', shared__txt='theirs\n')
o.push()
c = GitRepo.at(clone(str(bare), other, 'third'))
sh(c.root, 'config', 'user.email', 'tests@example.com')
sh(c.root, 'config', 'user.name', 'Repo tests')
sh(c.root, 'reset', '--hard', 'HEAD~1')
commit(c.root, 'ours', shared__txt='ours\n')
d = c.divergence()
test_eq(d['relation'], 'diverged')
test_eq(d['recommended'], 'merge')
test_eq({x['op']: x for x in d['options']}['rebase']['conflict_likely'], True)
```

`history` returns at most 500 commits, so the rebase rehearsal takes its
commits from `_to_replay`, which has no cap. A branch 600 commits ahead
of its upstream is rehearsed in full:

``` python
r6 = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'a.txt': 'base\n'}))
base, tree = r6._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD'), r6._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD^{tree}')
up = r6.run('commit-tree', tree, '-p', base, '-m', 'upstream').strip()
r6.run('update-ref', 'refs/heads/up', up)
head = base
for i in range(600): head = r6.run('commit-tree', tree, '-p', head, '-m', f'c{i}').strip()
r6.run('update-ref', 'HEAD', head)
rows = r6._to_replay(up, head)
test_eq((len(rows), rows[0]['subject'], rows[-1]['subject']), (600, 'c0', 'c599'))
rebase = {x['op']: x for x in r6.divergence('up')['options']}['rebase']
test_eq((rebase['replayed'], rebase['stops_at']), (600, None))
rebase['replayed']
```

## Ignore rules a folder needs

A folder without a suitable `.gitignore` stages build output such as
`target/`, `dist/`, `__pycache__` and `node_modules` along with the
work. `IGNORE_KINDS` describes four kinds of project: Rust, maturin (a
Python package built from Rust), Python and Node. For each it lists the
files that mark a folder as that kind, paths that must end up ignored,
and the rules to add when they are not.
[`project_kinds`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#project_kinds)
returns the kinds a folder holds. A folder holds `maturin` when it has
both `pyproject.toml` and `Cargo.toml`. A folder holds any other kind
when it has any one of that kind’s marker files. A `maturin` folder is
not also listed as `python`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1789"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### project_kinds

``` python
def project_kinds(
    folder
):
```

*Which kinds of project this folder holds, by the files that declare
one.*

``` python
d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); _tmp.append(str(d))
test_eq(project_kinds(d), [])
(d/'package.json').write_text('{}')
test_eq(project_kinds(d), ['node'])
(d/'Cargo.toml').write_text('[package]\n')
test_eq(project_kinds(d), ['rust', 'node'])             # marker order is `IGNORE_KINDS` order
(d/'pyproject.toml').write_text('[project]\n')
project_kinds(d)                                        # a crate plus a pyproject is maturin, not python
```

`missing_ignores(repo, folder)` returns a list of `(kind, lines)` pairs,
one for each kind of the folder whose probe paths Git does not already
ignore. It runs each probe path through `git check-ignore`. A
`.gitignore` written by hand with different rules therefore counts when
it covers the probe paths.
[`missing_ignores`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#missing_ignores)
writes nothing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1808"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### missing_ignores

``` python
def missing_ignores(
    repo, folder
):
```

*The `(kind, lines)` this folder needs and the repository does not
already cover.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
(r.root/'crate').mkdir(); (r.root/'crate'/'Cargo.toml').write_text('[package]\n')
test_eq([k for k, _ in missing_ignores(r, r.root/'crate')], ['rust'])
test_eq(_ignored(r, r.root/'crate'/'target'/'debug'/'build'), False)
write(r.root, '.gitignore', 'crate/target/\n')
test_eq(_ignored(r, r.root/'crate'/'target'/'debug'/'build'), True)
test_eq(missing_ignores(r, r.root/'crate'), [])         # already covered, in a shape of its own
test_eq(_ignored(r, '/elsewhere'), False)               # outside the worktree is never ignored
(r.root/'pyproject.toml').write_text('[project]\n')
missing_ignores(r, r.root)
```

[`prepare_ignores`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#prepare_ignores)
adds the missing rules to the folder’s own `.gitignore`, not the one at
the repository’s root. A root rule `/target/` does not match
`crate/target/`, so rules written there for a crate in a subfolder would
ignore nothing. A crate that carries its own ignore file also keeps it
when moved into another repository. `write=False` reports what it would
add without writing.
[`prepare_ignores`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#prepare_ignores)
returns a dictionary with `kinds` (the kinds that lacked rules), `added`
(the lines written, or the lines it would write when `write=False`) and
`path` (the `.gitignore` file). It skips lines that are already in the
file, and `added` is empty when the rules are already there. That is the
usual case on a second run.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1819"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### prepare_ignores

``` python
def prepare_ignores(
    repo, folder, write:bool=True
):
```

*Give `folder` the ignore rules its project kinds need, and say what was
added.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
(r.root/'web').mkdir(); (r.root/'web'/'package.json').write_text('{}')
dry = prepare_ignores(r, r.root/'web', write=False)
test_eq(dry['kinds'], ['node'])
test_eq((r.root/'web'/'.gitignore').exists(), False)    # write=False writes nothing

done = prepare_ignores(r, r.root/'web')
test_eq(done['added'], ['# Node', 'node_modules/', '*.tsbuildinfo'])
test_eq((r.root/'web'/'.gitignore').read_text(), '# Node\nnode_modules/\n*.tsbuildinfo\n')
test_eq(prepare_ignores(r, r.root/'web')['added'], [])  # the second run has nothing to add
(r.root/'web'/'node_modules').mkdir(); (r.root/'web'/'node_modules'/'x').write_text('x')
test_eq(_ignored(r, r.root/'web'/'node_modules'/'x'), True)  # the folder's own rules now cover it
done
```
